claims.text: The initial FeCoNi alloy is a single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy.
Severe plastic deformation by high-pressure torsion will refine the grains of FCC FeCoNi.
The high-pressure-torsion treatment is to be conducted at room temperature.
Grain refinement can introduce a secondary phase in the treated alloy.
Severe plastic deformation can transform an FCC high-entropy alloy into HCP and BCC-containing material.
Internal boundaries and dislocation slip can trigger an FCC-to-HCP transformation in a compositionally related alloy.
Reducing grain size increases the density of grain boundaries that pin magnetic domain walls.
Increased magnetic-domain-wall pinning raises the coercive field.
High-pressure-torsion grain refinement will raise the coercive field of FeCoNi above 100 Oe.
The single-phase FCC FeCoNi baseline has a coercive field no greater than 100 Oe.
Grain refinement may affect saturation magnetization.
Severe plastic deformation may introduce defects.
Severe plastic deformation may introduce impurities.

contradictions.description: The headline hypothesis presents introduction of a secondary phase as central, but the specified intervention and mediator only define grain refinement and do not identify the secondary phase or require that one form.

The falsification rule equates failure to increase coercivity with Hc ≤ 100 Oe. If the baseline is below 100 Oe, a treated sample could increase relative to baseline while remaining at or below 100 Oe, so the two conditions are not equivalent.
